exposure: Maternal characteristics (age, race, Medicaid income eligibility, county Medicaid enrollment, trimester prenatal care entry)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of patients from 2017 Alabama Medicaid administrative claims, with a focus on low-income patients, particularly those with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy (HDP) diagnosis.
finding: Black patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) had an elevated risk of severe maternal morbidities (SMM) compared with White patients with HDP, even after controlling for other maternal characteristics.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 2017 administrative claims.
